name: Hyde Park - Walk to University of Chicago
description:
If you are fully vaccinated, and able to climb 30 steps, you are invited to be the sole Airbnb guest in my quiet, vintage, 2nd floor apartment shared only with me. This Hyde Park location is convenient for visiting The University of Chicago or attending a convention/conference at McCormick Place. The listing is a block from the eastern border of UChicago, a 7 minute walk to Chicago Theological Seminary, and a 16 minutes door-to-door ride to McCormick Place via the Metra Electric train.

The space
The private bedroom has a queen size bed, bedside tables w/lamps, a chest of drawers, a desk and chair, and a smart TV. The large closet contains plenty of hangers, an iron and ironing board, a garment steamer, and extra bedding. There is room in the large closet to store your luggage.

All bedding (including mattress pad and duvet cover or quilt) is freshly laundered for each guest. During extended stays, weekly housekeeping is provided to the guest room at n
neighborhood_overview:
The apartment is less than one block from beautiful Jackson Park which houses the Museum of Science and Industry and the Japanese Gardens, built for the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition. Theaters, restaurants, grocery stores, book stores, and lakefront bicycle/running paths are within walking distance. This Hyde Park location is served by both the city and UChicago police departments.

My building is located almost next door to the Metra Electric train station, providing you with quick and inexpensive transportation to downtown Chicago. You need to be aware that the tradeoff for this convenience is the noise from occasional passing freight trains.
host_about:
My 2 bdrm apartment is a 2nd floor walk-up in a quiet, vintage co-op building, overlooking a pleasant courtyard.  I allow only one guest so you don't have to worry about other strangers in the apartment. (I occupy the 2nd bedroom).  A single traveler will feel safe and be comfortable here. If you are visiting the University of Chicago - or visiting your UChicago student who hasn't enough room to host you - my location will allow you to walk to your destination. My apartment is probably the Airbnb listing most convenient to the Chicago Theological Seminary. 

If you have been skeptical about  trying Airbnb, you will be pleasantly surprised at how drama-free the experience can be. The key is to read the listing (including house rules) and the reviews, then select a place that meets your safety, location, and comfort needs.

Let me know the purpose of your trip to Chicago so I can help you determine if my apartment or Hyde Park location is (or isn't) right for your visit.  I may even be able to suggest a more appropriate location. In any event, I will answer your inquiries quickly and honestly.

Clean and comfortable one-bedroom garden apartment with kitchenette in a vintage brick building. Sleeps 2-4 comfortably (queen bed and futon or air mattress). Pleasant and lively neighborhood and a short walk to the train.

The space
Garden apartment with private entry, one large bedroom, full bathroom, and kitchenette (microwave, coffee maker, toaster, mini-fridge, but no stove). Very fun and walkable neighborhood. Old Town School of Folk Music, Lincoln Square shopping/restaurants, grocery store, nearby train and bike sharing stations, parks, and more. We adhere to the Airbnb cleaning protocol and a minimum of 24 hours between guest stays.

There is no central air conditioning, but the apartment generally stays cool in warm weather; however, we do provide a portable air conditioner for the hot months. Of interest to families with youngsters, there is a little play area and toys under the stairs (Kids love it), a fun tree swing out front in the parkway
neighborhood_overview:
In our humble opinion, this is one of the best neighborhoods in Chicago. It's lively, fun and one of the safest in the city.

Within three blocks we have: independent coffee shop, an L station, Harvestime (eclectic, independent grocery store), bike/walking path along Chicago River, Bloom Yoga studio. Within 6-8 blocks: River Park w/ public pool, Waters School (w/natural prairie and community gardens). There's almost always something happening in Lincoln Square; check out the Chamber of Commerce events calendar online (sorry, can't provide links here.)

A note about crime and safety: The shootings in Chicago are concentrated in the south and west side neighborhoods; it can and does happen in all neighborhoods, but victims are almost always gang-involved. Situational awareness is always advised. We have never had any guests raise safety concerns, but we do want to help if you have any.
host_about: My family of four lives in the top unit of the two-flat. We spend a lot of time walking or biking around in our neighborhood (we happily have no car). You can often find us out front, sitting on the bench, swinging  from the tree, or just chatting with neighbors. We love visiting other cities where we can stay in interesting neighborhoods without the hassle of needing a car. We think our place is well-suited for others  who appreciate urban neighborhoods.

The space
:: Hi there and welcome to my listing! ::

name: The Stained Glass Apt. Edgewater #1
description:
The space
*Attention to first time users of Airbnb* This is not a private apartment for rent. I live here and I also have another smaller room listed on the site! My apartment is on the third floor of a three flat brick building on a quiet tree lined street in Edgewater. It was built 1916 in Prairie style featuring high ceilings, amazing woodwork and stained glass all of which have been restored. I'm a big fan of flea markets and antique stores so my home is filled with beautiful curiosities. My friend calls it "The museum" but don't let that scare you :) The place has a really comfy and peaceful vibe. It is spacious and open in the way that one can stand at one end of the apartment and see through to the other end. There is an enclosed sunporch in the front of the house which offers a serene view of the tops of trees. The bedroom I can offer has a comfortable double bed and a most prized Eastlake antique dresser with egyptian pharaoh head drawer pulls. There is one shared
neighborhood_overview: The location is really prime as it's approximately a 4 1/2 block walk (roughly 8 minutes) to either Granville or Loyola redline train stations as well as 6 blocks to the lake. The neighborhood is really lovely and down right lush with trees and flowers (when weather permits)  Although Edgewater is a 30-45 minute train ride downtown, there is something to be said for staying here and getting a taste of a real Chicago neighborhood. Staying downtown is great in many ways but it is the typical tourist view and you will not experience  what I consider to be the real heart of Chicago where the regular folks live. There are two antique malls, a couple of great coffee houses and restaurants all a short walk away.
host_about:
I am currently on a new path=which really means I lost my job and I want to try something different. I have done quite a bit of international travel and hope to do a lot more. I love people. I am an artist, card maker and writer. I am obsessed with postcards. I'm really in love with Chicago and although I've lived here my whole life I continue to discover new treasure!

Some things that I love: Writing, reading, bicycling, coffee, trying different types of food, yoga, movies, old cemeteries, art museums, photography, vintage postcards, pen pals, architecture, antique markets, folk art, tiles, decorative metal, wine, beer, and a well crafted cocktail and of course,  traveling!!!

I believe good things can come from seemingly bad things: the symbolic opening of a new door. 

I strive to be present, recognize beauty, project love, and be extremely grateful for my life.  Each person I meet reinforces my belief in a world full of love and kindness and every new friend makes it a better place.  Traveling has been my most valuable education. 

Places I have traveled: Austria, Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, England, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Kenya, Mexico, Monaco, Morocco, Netherlands, Peru, Poland, Portugal, Scotland, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Thailand, Turkey, Wales

Hi, we're Bob and Liz Biddle, long time Chicagoans and your hosts. We started At Home Inn Chicago in 2000 as a reservation service for bed and breakfasts in Chicago, and have since evolved into one of the city's most-respected sources for vacation rentals, corporate housing, and weekend getaways. 

We provide fully furnished vacation rentals and corporate housing throughout the city in or near Old Town and Lincoln Park.

We are here to answer all of your questions about Chicago, whether you need a restaurant recommendation, public transit tips, or insider tips on how to experience the Chicago that locals know and love. 

We love this city, especially getting ribs at Twin Anchors in Old Town before a show at Second City.  Topo Gigio is a great local Italian Restaurant and The Gemini Bistro is an excellent choice for fine dining. And Velvet Taco, casual with its own unique style on Lincoln is fabulous!

The free concerts at Pritzker Pavilion in Millenium Park can't be matched by any city in the world. 

We'd love to help you experience all of this with us and so much more!

neighborhood_overview: Pilsen is our favorite neighborhood in Chicago and is in the midst of dramatic change - hopefully change that retains the vibrant Mexican culture that makes it what it is. This is an artistic and culinary mecca for Chicago, with galleries throughout the neighborhood, politically and socially conscious murals on every block, and a wide array of food, including some of Chicago's best Mexican cuisine. The Mexican Fine Arts Museum is one of the best in the country. Several breweries are located here, along with dive bars, comedy spots, upscale fusion restaurants and music and mole festivals throughout the warm months. This is a demographically diverse community that is still dominated by Mexican families, but has a strong hipster and young professional presence as well. Get ready for Portlandia style beards and coiffed dogs.

host_about:
Who would have thought when I boarded a plane for Greece more than 20 years ago, planning on backpacking through the mountains and then heading north through then Yugoslavia I'd end up making Greece my second home?
But here I am, 20 something years later, running a fabulous Greek vacation rental business with historic homes & penthouses in Athens, planning Greek travel itineraries and leading small group food & wine focused tours around my adopted homeland and loving the life that I am lucky enough to be living. Of course I did pick up an equally crazy, workaholic Greek husband along the way, as well as a stray Greek animal or two!

Update: End of November 2017 .... This year Basil and I celebrate 15 years opening our Greek vacation rentals to guests from around the world. All these years we've been hopping between Basil's home city, Athens and Carole's home city of Chicago.  Time and time again guests in Greece ask us if they can stay in our Chicago home while we're in Athens.... so we're finally doing it - we've just completed the renovation of a fab old factory with 3 vacation rentals called the Magic Factory Lofts. We've got 3 and 4 bedroom homes in the heart of the city with Big Shoulders -  in our hybrid warehouse (which in a previous life housed a bar and a dance hall, followed by a costume and magic card factory and then a photography studio where probably every Butterball turkey advertisement in the 1980s was shot .... the photos, not the turkeys!)

So come stay with us ... and then stay with us again. Whether we share an ouzo in Athens in our Acropolis View Alpha Plus penthouse or Sky Villa or a beer and a hot dog in Chicago, in our Magic Factory Lofts  we know that you won't be disappointed.

neighborhood_overview:
McKinley Park has long been a working-class area throughout its history. Two blocks to the south along Pershing is the historic Central Manufacturing District. It has been described as the United States' first planned industrial district and features some surprisingly decorative warehouses from the turn of the century as well as an old clock tower. The juxtaposition of a city park on one side of Pershing with old huge seven story warehouses on the other is incredibly unique and worth scoping out.

The McKinley Park neighborhood is more of a quiet refuge from the night life scenes Chicago has to offer. You'll have to venture a little further for restaurants or bars. Pilsen to the north and Brideport to the east are excellent destinations for restaurants and Chicago's China town is a quick trip down the Orange line.

host_about:
I am a mother of an seventh year old son and we travel the world together.  I am a teacher of students with specials needs so I am a very patient person.  I love to be in nature to feel the energy of the sun and breeze and watch the birds and other animals. I need to be outside daily.  I walk each dog each day to the beach even in ten below zero weather.  The ice formations were amazing this winter on lake Michigan.  I used to try to complete two triathlons per year.  I practice yoga and have been doing this since studying in India over twenty years ago.  I am currently a crew member and race weekly during boating season and have completed in 5 Chicago to Mackinac island race.  I have fun with my family skiing and sailing our 24  foot San Juan in the summer, going out to the movies, or the opera, or a bike ride along Chicago's lake front or just playing charades at home.  I enjoy reading but lately most of my spare time is spent in the garden and home improvement projects.  I am passionate about my students and I would like to take a group of inner city student to Europe.  This is one of my educational dreams. 
I am Jamaican.  I visit home to see my mother some times.  My son's father is from southern Italy so we eat pasta often :) .  I speak Patios, some Spanish, Italian and German and English.  I love getting lost in nature and meeting people from differing cultures and countries.  And I like adventure.  We once drove from Chicago to New York for Christmas to see my family, then from New Your through Mexico, El Salvador and Guatemala to Honduras to see my son's father family and back to Chicago.  That was my longest road trip.  I have done some short treks in the Himalayas in Nepal and India, I have done some scuba diving in the Great Barrier Reef and have ridden a motorcycle across the US. The rest you can find when you visit, or not, I am happy either way.  If you visit during sailing season you are invited to go sailing with us.  
Happy trails and I wish you a happy and amazing life.

Airbnb Community Leader Host.
Art For Life Chicago, a non-profit organization. Founder and Philanthropist.

Laid back, down to earth professional.  Volunteerism is healthy for the soul.

Good luck.

host_about:
Hi!  :)  I'm Jason- a friendly, hyperactive, short and energetic fellow from the MidWest who loves building stuff and going places.  I'm a "people-person" from a family of world travelers; 4th generation Chicago cityboy with experience working in museums, hotels and ecolodges around the globe. 
Chicago history, architecture, and preservation are big interests of mine, and I take great pride in caring for the historic properties my family has lived in, owned & maintained for decades. 

I love AirBnb.  We have traveled, backpacked, hiked, camped, hoteled moteled, couch-surfed and home-shared... But AirBnb has been the single best thing to happen to us in our adult lives.

When we travel, we turn to AirBnb first, whether internationally, nationally, and in our own hometown.  From the glitzy new city experience to weekend trip to some small town in the country, we prefer staying with those in the AirBnb community.  The experience is always unique and always more authentic.

We are AirBnb hosts and consider it central to our lives here in Chicago.  Because my family lives in Chicago, one of us is always in the city, often while the rest of us travel. Any repairs are handled immediately. A while back, when I was moving from the building we own, we decided to open it for AirBnB guests. Now we have progressed to having vacation rentals within the building where we live.  Living upstairs with my son allows us to keep in great touch with our guests, maintaining the gardens and accommodations ourselves, as well as hosting occasional art, music and dining events. 

I love this way of traveling and hosting; meeting the folks who come to stay with us is precisely what fuels me on the day-to-day, and it's what makes our vacations so much more enjoyable!  We've met hundreds of incredible people and stayed in fantastic homes across the world.  AirBnb has been such a great chapter in our lives!  :)

neighborhood_overview:
Parks galore in Hyde Park! Walk 15 minutes east and you hit the Lake Shore trail which can make for a very relaxing morning. Stroll over to historic Jackson Park, home of the 1896 World's Fair. There are also numerous coffee shops and a wide variety of restaurants. Enjoy close proximity to the University of Chicago and all of its unique cultural offerings including the Oriental Institute Museum, the Smart Museum of Art, the Renaissance Museum, and of course, the beautiful architecture in and around campus. Also within walking distance are the Museum of Science and Industry and the Dusables Museum of African American History.

Hyde Park is a great place for those who want to explore the city but step away from the chaos at night and see one of the few remaining diverse neighborhoods of Chicago.

host_about:
I am a divorced father of four. That's my three youngest kids in the scooter sidecar with me. My oldest is all grown up and just graduated from law school in Texas. 
I worked for Apple. I currently consult with companies about technology/internet/social media/marketing/branding. We own the entire building and I work and live (some of the time) on the third floor with tenants on first floor. We use AirBnB for the Garden Apartment (totally private); the second floor is a hostel style AirBnB; and upstairs on the 3rd floor we have up to two bedrooms that are available when I don’t have my kids in town.
I enjoy going on bike rides to the beach with my kids, and my girlfriend and her kids. I love to read and I am a tech geek. I am a coffee OR tea drinker and after drinking both black for almost forty years, I have started using cream in them — a habit I picked up in Nairobi, Kenya a couple years ago when I was doing some missionary work (plus my girlfriend uses cream and so I have no choice). 
If I had to pick some things I can't live without: my girlfriend (and her boys); my kids; my technology; my morning coffee; my fellowship; and my friends. And I love to watch movies. Old. New. Comedy. Mystery. Action. It doesn't matter. I like them all. 
I enjoy working out — lifting weights and riding a bike, plus I am a life-long swimmer. I also just started playing hockey! At age 52! Crazy. 
We have been hosting guests for over five years now. We have over 250 reviews 98% are 5 star. We are a SuperHost. We love this. And we are really good at it.
I am a pretty laid back guy. I like things to be neat and tidy, but it's hard to do without motivation. AirBnB has been the motivation to get our place all tricked out and we are very proud of it. We hope you will enjoy staying here. All of our units are in a great neighborhood—in a great city. We have lots of suggestions for fun stuff to do, not the typical touristy stuff, but cool Chicago things that Chicagoans like to do/see.

Wrigleyville is the lively little pocket in the Lakeview neighborhood that sits in the shadows of historic Wrigley Field, the second oldest stadium in baseball and home to the beloved Chicago Cubs. It has become a magnet for sports fans and young professionals alike, and particularly singles who hop from bar to bar along Clark, Addison and Sheffield Avenues.

Rather tame by day, the neighborhood's souvenir shops and casual eateries are open but quiet. For late night entertainment, a boisterous after-hours crowd heads to Wrigleyville for everything from live music to sketch comedy. Hi I'm Evelyn, a Chicago native who’s also lived in New York City where I ran my massage therapy practice and studio and worked with people in music, film, fashion and art.

I couldn't be happier about living in this location! Between being steps away from the beach, the friendly culturally diverse neighborhood, the up and coming restaurants, cafes, community run spaces and nightlife, I'm enjoying my lovely spacious nest and location.

In years past I've been a stylist and had a beautiful shop where I sold everything from vintage clothing, antique costumes from the Lyric Opera, kimonos and couture to art and vintage lifestyle items. I continue to style people mainly from my collection.

I spent four years running Open Secret Studios with the purpose of supporting art, culture and humanitarian causes. I rented out the space for photography, video and private events to support the things I care about. I became adept at providing a beautiful backdrop and supporting clients while keeping them happy before, during, and after event experiences. I hope to do the same for you . 

I am offering my home to travelers and am happy to give you space and share information about events going on around town. I have lived all over the city from Downtown to the Westside to Fulton Market and have found Rogers Park appealing on many levels without the pretension. I love living so close to the lake and look forward to discovering historic architecture on my walks through the neighborhood.

I practice yoga and meditation as well as swim, hike, bike, and make art in my  studio in the house. I make collage and mosaic from old ceramic pieces and plates found on beaches all over the world. I also work in textiles.

neighborhood_overview:
Neighborhoods:
Nearby are three vibrant nearby neighborhoods (Ravenswood, Lincoln Square & Andersonville). All have beautiful, tree-lined residential streets, as well as business areas filled with interesting shops, excellent restaurants, entertainment, and parks.
* Andersonville, originally a Swedish neighborhood, has a lot of unique and LGBT-owned businesses. Their Chamber of Commerce stresses buying local. We agree!
* Lincoln Square, originally a German neighborhood, has a European-flavor with interesting shops and terrific restaurants. It is also home to the Old Town School of Folk Music (offering classes & a huge range of concerts, including folk, jazz, Celtic, & World music).
* Ravenswood, originally an industrial district, is now the craft-beer corridor of Chicago, plus great restaurants, a vodka distillery, and fun shops. All three neighborhoods are safe, walkable areas. Public transportation to other parts of the city is readily available.
host_about:
David and his husband, William,  live in on the north side of Chicago. They've been a couple since 1980.  William grew up in Chicago while David grew up in suburban Denver. David attended graduate school in Iowa, then moved with William to Austin, Texas for two years. They both worked in western Connecticut for several years before moving to Chicago. They have lived in their current home since 1997.

David is a psychologist by training but spent the last half of his career as a higher education administrator. He is now retired! His leisure interests include music (especially acoustic singer-songwriters), baking, films, and books. William trained as a librarian. spent much of his career as an academic administrator, and is now works in the Human Resources department at the Old Town School of Folk Music. He also loves music, books, and films, but also enjoys baseball immensely (Go Cubs!) and running. \

They both love cats as well as traveling. Favorite trips include visits to Prague and Budapest (and a river cruise on the Danube), Paris, northern Italy, central & southern Spain, Vancouver, Montréal, New Mexico, and the Inside Passageway of Alaska (via a small cruise boat of 72 passengers). When traveling to big cities, they seek out neighborhoods where the locals live to get a better sense of day-to-day life for the people who reside there. The next big trip will be a river cruise on the Rhine from Amsterdam to Basel, Switzerland (with extra time in Lucerne). 

Both report they love living in this part of Chicago. Their home is nestled at the north end of the Ravenswood neighborhood and is within a 15- to 20-minute walk of both the Andersonville and Lincoln Square neighborhoods. That gives them access to a wealth of excellent restaurants, shopping, and a gorgeous park,  plus easy access to public transportation options (bus, CTA Brown line, and Metra UP North).

As hosts, they like to provide as comfortable a space as possible and offer information or recommendations as requested. They both love to chat with guests but also respect that some folks are seeking a refuge and just want to enjoy the space without a lot of conversation. 

When they travel, both love to seek out restaurants that reflect local cultures, visit museums, explore architecture of the area, as well as connect to locals. On a recent trip to Prague, they stayed in a lovely small studio apartment in a neighborhood several miles from the downtown tourist area. It was a great opportunity to see how the locals lived and to get a feel for what it might be like to live there.

host_about:
Miriam is a Chicagoan born & raised, while Carl hails from Sweden; the land of Vikings & Volvos, & the all-famous Abba.  We met while working abroad & recently relocated to Chicago to be closer to family & enjoy this fantastic city.

In 2016 we bought this 130+ year old historic greystone home.  We spent 18 months meticulously taking it apart one wooden beam at a time. After overhauling the heating, plumbing, & electric with the most efficient systems we could find, we then put it all back together - preserving as much of the original hardwood, bricks & beautiful finishes we possibly could. We found there is indeed truth to the phrase 'labor of love', and we couldn't be more proud of the work we've accomplished.  

Our professional careers revolve around sustainability & we try to lead our lives as close to our environmentally friendly values as we can while still leading modern, robust lives. We love spending as much outdoors time as the weather allows us;  hiking, gardening, skiing - we love it all. name: Cozy apartment in great Ukrainian Village
description:
Enjoy your Chicago stay in our vintage apartment which is centrally located near public transportation and near all the fun of Wicker Park, Logan Square and Ukrainian Village. You will have the place to yourself as we rent out our whole apartment when we are away.

The space
Enjoy your stay in our cozy vintage apartment located in the heart of Ukrainian Village / Wicker Park. Our apartment is on a very quiet tree lined street (for good night sleep) but within walking distance to all the buzzing restaurants, bars, cafes and live music venues the neighborhood has to offer. We are very close to public transportation (Western bus 49 & Damen and Western blue line stop)

Getting around //

-The Western bus stop (#49) is 2 walking minutes away from us and will easily connect you to the Western Blue line train stop. From there it’s a 15 min ride downtown. All in all ca 25 minutes.

- Getting here from O'Hare via public transit is very simple.
neighborhood_overview:
Ukrainian Village, Wicker Park and Logan Square are three of the best neighborhoods in Chicago because of their lively, hip and diverse atmosphere. There are a ton of bars and restaurants but also really sweet residential streets with awesome houses to look at. Humboldt Park is great for relaxing and/or jogging and just a five minute walk away. Supermarkets and little Delis are within walking distance.
O‘Hare is just a 40 Minute train ride away (blue line). Downtown you can reach within 30 minutes.
host_about:
Originally from Germany, this is year 4 of living and loving life in Chicago.

I love traveling and meeting people from all over the world while staying in airbnbs. When at home, I like to do the same - this is why I share my apartment and the things I love about Chicago with you - so you can have an amazing time here.

Interior design, music, cooking and eating, pastels colors, hyenas and hummus are amongst my favorite things to do.

Dining ranges from traditional comfort food to Turkish, burgers to bakeries, Cuban to creamy custards — all serving up casual hospitality.

host_about:
Hello, Travelers!  Welcome to your temporary home in Chicago!  We love our location near Hyde Park, the University of Chicago, the Lake and the Parks and just over 10 minutes to downtown Chicago via the Lake.  

Our family of four takes full advantage of the walking and bike trails in the area. We also frequent nearby Hyde Park, for its distinctive and unique offerings and to hopefully, run into a friend or two.

We still love road trips but, our favorite trips are with our extended family.  Recently, 20+ family members descended upon San Pedro, Belize and again in Costa Rica.  This year less exotic Washington, DC is on the list.

Because I have Lupus and Rheumatoid Arthritis I am an licensed Illinois Medical Cannabis patient.  I live a healthy lifestyle which includes living gluten-free and I encourage others to incorporate health into their lives.

The Spark Clubs is based on a wellness concept.   We do not allow tobacco because it is a known carcinogen and the chemicals affect the air quality of everyone in the building.  The smoke smell lays on the walls and soft goods, linens and curtains.  We have to spend extra money to clean that off when folks violate our rules. That is why we have a security deposit now to encourage good behavior.

When people use cannabis alone, there tends to be significantly less smell and it does not linger. With the ventilation methods we employ, any smoke can be quickly evacuated from the room.  As a result, our rooms stay fresh.  

As far as linens are concerned, we shopped for high-quality bedding to provide you with the best sleep experience you can find.  Our beds have toppers and pads and down comforters and feather pillows and percale sheets... all designed to make your sleep experience exceptional.  In order to maintain our investment in our linens, we ask that people refrain from smoking, eating or drinking in the bedrooms.  Each bed has around $420 in linens on it, this is why we ask for a deposit.  Typically the only damage we've had is smoke and linens.

The unit smells pleasant and you will sleep on high quality, freshly laundered linens.  

We all love to read and take books with us on vacation.  Sometimes we wing it, just start driving and book from the road with a last-minute hotel app.  Sometimes we plan a year in advance.

I'm a Super Host because I love hosting!  I am so into creating a great experience for people, I am looking forward to each and every guest.  I'm very friendly and talkative, however, I intend to disappear so guests can create their own memories.

One of my many mottos:  Eat dessert first.

Bridgeport, one of 77 community areas of Chicago, Illinois, is a neighborhood on the city's South Side. Bridgeport served as a shortcut for French traders who soon saw the economic potential for a canal. When Fort Dearborn was completed, what is now Bridgeport became Leigh's Place. Centered on James Leigh's farm, it became Chicago's first neighborhood. In 1836, the area was renamed Bridgeport.
Historically, much of the neighborhood began as an Irish-American enclave. In the 1830s, large numbers of immigrants from Ireland started settling in this working-class neighborhood. Many of the same Irish immigrants who helped build the Erie Canal later came to Chicago to work on the Illinois and Michigan Canal. host_about:
I am a divorced father of four. That's my three youngest kids in the scooter sidecar with me. My oldest is all grown up and just graduated from law school in Texas. 
I worked for Apple. I currently consult with companies about technology/internet/social media/marketing/branding. I enjoy working out — lifting weights and riding a bike, plus I am a life-long swimmer. I also just started playing hockey! At age 52! Crazy.

We hope you will enjoy staying here. All of our units are in a great neighborhood—in a great city. Join us at Freehand Chicago Hotel for your travels in Chicago. Perfect for travelers here too long for a traditional hotel or for just 1 night; make us your home away from home.

This listing is for one bunk for one person in a shared mixed/co-ed room with 4 bunks (up to 3 roommates). We have many options such as private standard rooms and private quad rooms. Please send us a message with any questions.

$5 nightly resort fee plus tax paid at the property

The space
Somewhere between a hostel and hotel, you'll find the amenities you need to get through anywhere from a week to a few months. This listing is for one twin bunk in a shared room with four total bunks, so you would have up to 3 roommates. The room has a private bathroom and lockers for storing valuables. Each bunk features a curtain for privacy, reading lamp, and power outlet. Linens and towels are included, as is regular housekeeping service. Guests are welcome to use their own locks
neighborhood_overview: The Freehand Chicago is near the corner of Ohio and State st. It is downtown in the heart of River North, 1 block from the Magnificent Mile, 1 block across the River from The Loop, and a quick walk, bus, train, or taxi to anywhere you need to go.  We are also conveniently located across the street from Jewel, a major grocery store chain.
host_about:
Freehand Chicago is housed in a 1927 building in Chicago’s vibrant River North neighborhood – home to some of the city’s best art galleries, boutiques and restaurants.

Freehand is a collection of hotels that combine the social culture of a hostel with innovative design, award-winning food and beverage, and a community-driven atmosphere. Each Freehand takes its cues from the surrounding neighborhood, with spaces that are a microcosm of the best each city has to offer.

name: Sonder | The Plymouth | One-Bedroom Apartment
description:
A hop from some of the finest museums in the country, a skip from Grant Park, and a jump from the mouthwatering menus of South Loop's best restaurants and bars. The Plymouth puts you in the heart of the Windy City action. And with a Divvy Bike station on your doorstep and a subway stop around the corner, everything else for your prime Chicago experience is just a short ride away. Strolling down South Dearborn, you can't miss the art-deco-lettered sign or ornate facade of the building. Cozy up in the lounge or recline on the rooftop to unwind after your travels. Then take in the city skyline view over a shared meal at the grilling area. Freshen up in your comfortable space before you hop, skip, and jump into your city adventure.

The space
Working, relaxing, living. Our spaces have all the other essentials you need for your stay.

- Contact-free check-in
- 24/7 virtual support
- Super-fast WiFi
- Fresh towels and bathroom essentials
neighborhood_overview: The South Loop is a vibrant blend of notable attractions, beautiful parks, and stunning Lake Michigan views. Picnic in the charming green space surrounding Museum Campus, or attend one of the many events at Grant Park such as The Taste of Chicago. Spend the day exploring the countless museums, or journey to the top of the 108-story Willis Tower for breathtaking views of the city.

As a host I strive to help my guests experience all the things I love about the cities and towns that I love - the food, culture and  natural beauty - in comfortable accommodations that are reasonably priced. Avondale’s long industrial focus has evolved through the years, and today you can find breweries – and even a collaborative working space for makers.

“Featuring streets lined with hip galleries and walls decorated with colorful murals dating from the 1970s, the Pilsen neighborhood on Chicago’s Lower West Side is a nest of cutting-edge culture and art,” says Biggs Bradley. “It’s been fostered by successive waves of Eastern European and Mexican immigrants, in addition to local artists and students, who have molded this fascinating area over the past century and a half. host_about:
I am a divorced father of four. That's my three youngest kids in the scooter sidecar with me. My oldest is all grown up and just graduated from law school in Texas. 
I worked for Apple. I currently consult with companies about technology/internet/social media/marketing/branding. If I had to pick some things I can't live without: my girlfriend (and her boys); my kids; my technology; my morning coffee; my fellowship; and my friends. And I love to watch movies. Old. New. Comedy. Mystery. Action. It doesn't matter. I like them all. 
I enjoy working out — lifting weights and riding a bike, plus I am a life-long swimmer. I also just started playing hockey! At age 52! Crazy. 
We have been hosting guests for over five years now. We have over 250 reviews 98% are 5 star. We are a SuperHost. We love this. And we are really good at it.
I am a pretty laid back guy. I like things to be neat and tidy, but it's hard to do without motivation. AirBnB has been the motivation to get our place all tricked out and we are very proud of it. We hope you will enjoy staying here. All of our units are in a great neighborhood—in a great city. We have lots of suggestions for fun stuff to do, not the typical touristy stuff, but cool Chicago things that Chicagoans like to do/see.

Back of the Yards is an industrial and residential neighborhood so named because it was near the former Union Stock Yards, which employed thousands of European immigrants in the early 20th century. Life in this neighborhood was explored in Upton Sinclair's 1906 novel The Jungle. The area was formerly part of the town of Lake until it was annexed by Chicago in 1889. Hello, Travelers!  Welcome to your temporary home in Chicago!  We love our location near Hyde Park, the University of Chicago, the Lake and the Parks and just over 10 minutes to downtown Chicago via the Lake.  

Our family of four takes full advantage of the walking and bike trails in the area. We also frequent nearby Hyde Park, for its distinctive and unique offerings and to hopefully, run into a friend or two.

We still love road trips but, our favorite trips are with our extended family.  Recently, 20+ family members descended upon San Pedro, Belize and again in Costa Rica.  This year less exotic Washington, DC is on the list.

Because I have Lupus and Rheumatoid Arthritis I am an licensed Illinois Medical Cannabis patient.  I live a healthy lifestyle which includes living gluten-free and I encourage others to incorporate health into their lives.

The Spark Clubs is based on a wellness concept.   We do not allow tobacco because it is a known carcinogen and the chemicals affect the air quality of everyone in the building.  The smoke smell lays on the walls and soft goods, linens and curtains.  We have to spend extra money to clean that off when folks violate our rules. That is why we have a security deposit now to encourage good behavior.

When people use cannabis alone, there tends to be significantly less smell and it does not linger. With the ventilation methods we employ, any smoke can be quickly evacuated from the room.  As a result, our rooms stay fresh.  

As far as linens are concerned, we shopped for high-quality bedding to provide you with the best sleep experience you can find.  Our beds have toppers and pads and down comforters and feather pillows and percale sheets... all designed to make your sleep experience exceptional.  In order to maintain our investment in our linens, we ask that people refrain from smoking, eating or drinking in the bedrooms.  Each bed has around $420 in linens on it, this is why we ask for a deposit.  Typically the only damage we've had is smoke and linens.

The unit smells pleasant and you will sleep on high quality, freshly laundered linens.  

We all love to read and take books with us on vacation.  Sometimes we wing it, just start driving and book from the road with a last-minute hotel app.  Sometimes we plan a year in advance.

I'm a Super Host because I love hosting!  I am so into creating a great experience for people, I am looking forward to each and every guest.  I'm very friendly and talkative, however, I intend to disappear so guests can create their own memories.

One of my many mottos:  Eat dessert first.

host_about:
I am a mother of an seventh year old son and we travel the world together.  I am a teacher of students with specials needs so I am a very patient person.  I love to be in nature to feel the energy of the sun and breeze and watch the birds and other animals. I need to be outside daily.  I walk each dog each day to the beach even in ten below zero weather.  The ice formations were amazing this winter on lake Michigan.  I used to try to complete two triathlons per year.  I practice yoga and have been doing this since studying in India over twenty years ago.  I am currently a crew member and race weekly during boating season and have completed in 5 Chicago to Mackinac island race.  I have fun with my family skiing and sailing our 24  foot San Juan in the summer, going out to the movies, or the opera, or a bike ride along Chicago's lake front or just playing charades at home.  I enjoy reading but lately most of my spare time is spent in the garden and home improvement projects.  I am passionate about my students and I would like to take a group of inner city student to Europe.  This is one of my educational dreams. 
I am Jamaican.  I visit home to see my mother some times.  My son's father is from southern Italy so we eat pasta often :) .  I speak Patios, some Spanish, Italian and German and English.  I love getting lost in nature and meeting people from differing cultures and countries.  And I like adventure.  We once drove from Chicago to New York for Christmas to see my family, then from New Your through Mexico, El Salvador and Guatemala to Honduras to see my son's father family and back to Chicago.  That was my longest road trip.  I have done some short treks in the Himalayas in Nepal and India, I have done some scuba diving in the Great Barrier Reef and have ridden a motorcycle across the US. The rest you can find when you visit, or not, I am happy either way.  If you visit during sailing season you are invited to go sailing with us.  
Happy trails and I wish you a happy and amazing life.

I am passionate about my students and I would like to take a group of inner city student to Europe.  This is one of my educational dreams.

I love getting lost in nature and meeting people from differing cultures and countries.  And I like adventure.  We once drove from Chicago to New York for Christmas to see my family, then from New Your through Mexico, El Salvador and Guatemala to Honduras to see my son's father family and back to Chicago.  That was my longest road trip.  I have done some short treks in the Himalayas in Nepal and India, I have done some scuba diving in the Great Barrier Reef and have ridden a motorcycle across the US. Happy trails and I wish you a happy and amazing life.

host_about:
Hi, I'm Lynette.  I'm originally from Texas, but have spent most of my life in California, Colorado and now in Chicago.  I've kind of been a nomad all my life. I moved here 13 years ago looking for a big city that still felt comfy.  I found it!  I absolutely love this city!  My husband, Efrain, is Puerto Rican and lived here all his life.  We come from really different backgrounds, but that's why our life is so dynamic.

We love to travel...we've been to Mexico, Brazil, Costa Rica, Thailand, Spain and all over the United States.  

My husband and I bought this beautiful building and want to share our great neighborhood with lots of folks.  This is one of the most walkable neighborhoods in Chicago, with beautiful tree lined streets.  It's the Chicago we know and love.

We love music, art, design.  We love talking to people from different backgrounds and cultures and so we really appreciate seeing things through other people's eyes.  

We love all kinds of food - maybe too much now that we're getting older!!  That's why we love this neighborhood - you can have Afghan, Puerto Rican, Columbian and lots of Farm to Table all in one area!! Oh and plenty of greasy diner food too!

When we travel, we like to pick the location and the place we'll stay and wing it from there - not too overthought or planned.  That way, we can get a feel for the place and take it from there.  When our boys were little we took them to Costa Rica for Christmas with only small school backpack on their backs.  We landed in San Jose and asked them "which way should we go?"  - East or West.  WE chose east and went on the most amazing adventure with them all the to the Coast.

Last year, we went to Thailand and did everything from chill on the beach to staying on a river hotel to riding tuk tuks to the daily market.  WE like to meet new people and do a fair amount of people watching as well.  Our AirBnb host at the beach was so helpful in helping us get out and get around to places the other tourists weren't going...she helped us see her town with a fresh pair of eyes.

We are so excited to host people from other cities, other countries and other walks of life.  I love to hear a good travel story and love trying to learn new words in other languages. We both speak Spanish, my husband more than me!  

When we first got married, we brought our two families together - him with his kids and me with mine.  That was an amazing and intense time, and now our kids are teens and adults.  We're looking forward to this new phase of our lives and looking forward to the promise and adventure that lies ahead.

neighborhood_overview:
A boom in trendy restaurants has put the Fulton Market District in Chicago's Near West Side neighborhood on the foodie map -- with long waits to prove it.
Au Cheval, a dimly lit bar and restaurant on Randolph Street, boasts what's widely touted as the city's best burger.
The double stack, covered in oozing cheese, has inspired some committed patrons to wait for the few coveted tables or bar seats for up to three hours.
"Top Chef" winner Stephanie Izard's tapas restaurant Girl & the Goat also earns rave reviews. Making a weekend reservation two months out can be a feat, so some people opt for its casual sister spot, Little Goat.
The elaborately prepared cocktails and imaginative molecular gastronomy of The Aviary cocktail lounge have turned it into a Fulton staple.
Chef-owner Grant Achatz, of renowned restaurant Alinea, has created ingredient-infused cocktails in space-age barware that require user participation -- like cracking an ice egg -- before enjoying.

host_about:
Hello!  My name is Jennifer and I am the founder of Ovation Rentals, LLC which specializes in connecting hosts (including myself!) with guests looking for short- and long-term rental units in Chicago and Southwest Michigan.  We have something for everyone, from the unexpected visitor just needing a safe, comfortable place to rest her head to a family planning a big reunion on Lake Michigan.  

I am originally from Chicago, but when to college in UPENN in Philadelphia and also lived in New York before settling back in the Second City.  I have been a lover of travel for as long as I remember.  I took my first international trip  (to Paris!) when I was just 15 years old.  I made a deal with my dad that if I could save up the money for the flights by working 2 summer jobs then he would pay for the hotel and meals.  I worked my butt off that summer and we spent Christmas in Paris...and I was hooked on world travel!  Before Airbnb existed, I did much of my international travel via Home Exchange - where you exchange homes with a host family in another city (NOT the same as "couch surfing" lol).  I found that experiencing a new city like a local was infinitely more enjoyable than staying in a stuffy hotel, so when Airbnb came along I was overjoyed to have a new way to "live like a local!"  And eventually I evolved from just an Airbnb Traveler to an Airbnb Host.  

As a host I strive to help my guests experience all the things I love about the cities and towns that I love - the food, culture and  natural beauty - in comfortable accommodations that are reasonably priced.  I strive to do the same for the other hosts that I represent through Ovation.  Our goal is to make every guest feel truly at home!

For a feel of the youthful, creative energy on Chicago's northwest side, make your way to the eclectic cross-sections of West Town, Ukrainian Village and East Village. You'll pass colorful galleries and museums, independent theater companies, small-scale music venues and retail boutiques touting lines from local designers. Mixed in are historic churches, brick cottages, quaint coffee shops and a booming restaurant and bar scene.

Day and night, these communities offer a multitude of things to do, all with a low-key vibe and within an easy stroll. You'll have access to our kitchen, garden deck, beech tree lounge, and one of the most spectacular rooftop decks in Chicago!

You will be able to enjoy a private 1st floor suite, with a beautiful large, very comfortable living room, and private front door entrance. You could easily stay within walking distance of our house and have a fabulous, quintessentially Chicago neighborhood experience without ever getting in a car.  On a typical Saturday morning Kris and I often walk to La Boulangerie for coffee and the best crepes this side of Paris, and to buy our bread for the week. Otherwise, there are a dozen other choices for coffee and/or breakfast you can walk to. The food scene here is ridiculous. Thai? Probably a dozen choices. Burgers? Everywhere. Sushi? Of course. Chicago pizza? The famous Lou Malnati's is about 200 feet away. Korean? Best in Chicago, walking distance. All night diner? Just across the park. Awesome Jewish Deli? Super close. Traditional Southern? Don't dare miss Luella's Southern Kitchen, two blocks away. "Little India", on Devon Avenue, the most diverse street in Americ
host_about: My wife Kris and I love living in Lincoln Square, in Chicago. Kris has worked at a community college for 25 years and loves working with students. I have been a news cameraman for a local news station and have a photography business on the side. We love to travel both domestically and internationally. Our favorite things to do in the city involve going out to the many fabulous restaurants, enjoying live music at any of the wonderful venues, and doing yoga and exercising.. A major reason that we have signed up to host on Airbnb is that we love meeting new people and look forward to expanding our circle of friends!

Printers Row is “pocket” neighborhood between Congress Parkway and Polk Street just minutes from the Chicago Loop. host_about:
Hi, I'm a Chicago-based professional jazz musician with several albums out and a really gorgeous condo that is super-expensive to live in.  Hello, airbnb! I'm an excellent hostess and have dozens of testimonials on this site to back up that claim, so, please make your stay in Chicago with me and make a new friend in the process?  


Random tid-bits:

I love great wines, particularly full-bodied red wines.  And I love to share a great bottle with someone who has great insight to share.

I love thunderstorms and snowstorms-- I guess because they can mirror the tempestuous soul.

I detest smoke and find drug-use a huge turn-off; it just depresses me.  Neither are acceptable in my home or propinquity.

Can't cook.  Won't try.  Great at ordering take-out, though.

Hate the sound of clashing silverware.

Love children more than anything (!!!!) but I don't have a child-friendly condo.

Would rather have terminal cancer than a broken heart.

Jazz snob-- no, I don't think Norah Jones is a jazz singer, stop asking me to sing her stupid songs. (Sorry)  

You will hear plenty of Chet Baker, Monk, Anita O'Day, Ben Webster, Cannonball Adderly, Wes Montgomery, Carmen McRae, Sarah Vaughan, Mel Torme, Miles Davis, Oscar Peterson... you catch the drift, I'm a jazz-baby.

Love lots of genres of music (Blues, Celtic, Classical, folk, Middle Eastern, French cabaret, classic rock...) but really cannot tolerate rap or the current definition of R&B/soul.  Most pop past the 90's sucks.  (LOL... I am so making enemies here...)

I have more *friends* (not acquaintances-- FRIENDS) than anyone you may ever meet!  Literally.  It's a blessing.  My loyalty is deep and wide to people who are heartfelt and kind. ;)  Often, I like to have a few people over for wine, cheese, political discussions, chats about matters of the heart... Quiet company time is a favorite past time of mine.

I prefer the city-scape to the prairie.  I love a full moon.  I wear stilettos like an infant wears diapers- ALWAYS. ;-))

I love poetry and people who live poetic lives.

I am hopeless with most technology and miss things like phones with buttons.  My iphone is an irritation to me more than a beloved treasure.

People say I was born in the wrong era.  I agree.

Nothing better than a person with a quick and unique sense of humor and a compassionate, fearless heart. 

People show their true character when they think no one is looking.

Sports bars have taken over America.  That isn't a good thing.

There's nothing sexier than humility.

I'd rather be trusting and mistaken than safely pessimistic.    

If you can make grilled cheese you might as well be Charlie Trotter in my world.

Good parents are my favorite people.

Fashion is an expression of personality, but real beauty comes from within.

I am intolerant of intolerance.  Racism is the most disgusting characteristic of man.  

I like to box with my trainer in my pink boxing gloves, yet I was a ballet dancer more than half my life.

I'm allergic to most animals.  It's ridiculous how bad my allergies are.  So the cruel irony is I love animals but I avoid them like the plague or I'm sick for days.

Strangers on airplanes usually become friends with me-- or hate it when I fall asleep on their shoulder as they try to read... or sit comfortably in their own space. (LOL)

A goal is to learn several languages.  

Old people make my heart melt, and I often want to snuggle them like grandparents.  The lineage of history that dwells inside their eyes is a reminder to live a good, productive, grateful life. 

I prefer baths to showers and candlelight to sunlight.

I think Reality TV is one of the country's biggest embarrassments and teachers should earn what basketball players make in a career. 

I'm in awe of people who can draw, paint, sculpt, sew, build things... 

I do not know the difference between a baseball and a football.  (Kidding- but only slightly).  

If it's a choice between a tellurian wine bar/cafe OR the hot new stand-in-line for an hour nightclub?: Wine bar.  Even if I have VIP passes, free drinks all night, celebrity hosts-- those "scenes" of pick up joints and crowded clubs make me disengaged.  I prefer a half empty room at closing time with deep conversation. 

I have bouts of insomnia.  But I typically write in those times.

I like to clean and scrub the apartment-- it's cathartic.

I like people who are thoughtful, witty, compassionate and honest.   Clean and respectful is appreciated too.

People with dreams are common.  People that follow their dreams and sacrifice their comfort to pursue their deeper passions, with focused tenacity: they are the spice of life that inspires. 

You can tell a lot about a person by how they treat a waiter, a doorman, a busboy, a janitor and an assistant.

Money doesn't buy class.  Or good taste.

Beauty is in the eye of the beholder, and everyone is someone's child.

Everyone has a gift.

Music, at it's best, is a healer.

One genuine smile can change a stranger's entire day.

I'd rather be remembered as a loving person than an attractive one.

description:
Our house, located in Historic Pullman (National Monument), was built in 1881 by industrialist and creator of the Pullman sleeping car, George Pullman. While the interior is tastefully rehabbed, the exterior and community have the same charm of the late 1800s. If you love art, our home showcases art from local artists. Neighbors are friendly, the community is quiet and loaded with history. We will greet guests.

Our home is a getaway ....for out-of-town travelers!!

The space

neighborhood_overview:
Located on the southside of Chicago, Historic Pullman, designated a National Monument in 2015, offers a rich history of history on industrialization and the labor movement, and currently is enjoying exciting community revitalization. Private and group tours can be made by special arrangement. A self-guided tour with brochure is available. Stop by the Pullman Café for coffee, a pastry and sandwich or for comfort food at Cal-Habor Restaurant and Lounge, a neighborhood staple for more than 40 years!

Pullman also boasts of a Visitor's Center with a 15-minute introductory video on the town's history through today's preservation efforts, and exhibits featuring historic photos and Pullman-related items. The Visitor's Center, will open inside the Historic Pullman Clock Tower and Administration Building by Labor Day 2020.

Pullman Artspace Lofts, a new 38-unit development for artists, will be fully operational by the end of 2019.

The A. Philip Randolph P
host_about: My husband Melvin, an artist, and I, a creative, have lived in Pullman for over 20 years. We are both retired and are active members of Pullman's growing art community and currently sit on the Pullman Arts Board of Directors. We have witnessed phenomenal growth in Pullman since being designated a National Park in 2015, and are excited with visitors getting a chance to appreciate its almost 140-year history through walking tours, the Visitor Center, A. Philip Randolph Museum, and annual art, garden, and house walks, to name a few. We like to point out what makes Pullman special to us and want guests to feel comfortable while staying at our three-bedroom home. We're avid art enthusiast, which is evident with the art located on every wall. When we are not traveling, Melvin spends most days painting and volunteering for several human services agencies. I spend my time tinkering on projects around the house; I'm a closet carpenter and gardener until August, then every weed is a glorious flower.

host_about:
Love Travelers,  traveling and everything in between.  Born and raised in Chicago, we became avid travellers and barter enthusiasts. With over 20 years of travelling we could easily write our own book on travelling on a budget.  We PRIDE ourselves on the deals we obtain.  A week in Ireland, rental of two 3 bedroom entire homes for $45! FOUR Chicago Bull playoff games during the Michael Jordan Era included 4th row floor seats, box seats...$100 total!  Travelled europe thru 15 countries for $500 including accommodations and food...for a 3 month period!  And this was BEFORE Airbnb. We can go on.  We are geeked when we find a deal and become just plain silly with happiness at an unbelievable deal.  Even upon confirmation, our website for our guests are filled with free and things to do for CRAZY CHEAP.  'Spend like a spencer, but live like a king!'  

We feel everyone should open their minds to new things, cultural experiences and diversity.  Only then can you understand people thru their eyes and not some narrow minded media coverage.  By letting their experience be your experience will help you better understand people in a true and raw sense.  That's why we simply love Airbnb.  It places you in parts of the world where you probably wouldn't have gone but always wanted to go to get that 'local' feel with a local and trusted host.   

Since we don't travel as much as I used to....Let your experience be our experience!

We look forward to meeting you.

I am a mother of an seventh year old son and we travel the world together.  I am a teacher of students with specials needs so I am a very patient person. I love getting lost in nature and meeting people from differing cultures and countries.  And I like adventure.  We once drove from Chicago to New York for Christmas to see my family, then from New Your through Mexico, El Salvador and Guatemala to Honduras to see my son's father family and back to Chicago.  That was my longest road trip.  I have done some short treks in the Himalayas in Nepal and India, I have done some scuba diving in the Great Barrier Reef and have ridden a motorcycle across the US. Happy trails and I wish you a happy and amazing life.

neighborhood_overview:
The Alta Vista Terrace District, built in 1904, is a historic district in the Lake View community of Chicago, Illinois. Alta Vista Terrace was one of Samuel Eberly Gross’s last real estate developments. Inspired by a visit to Europe, Gross and architect Joseph C. Brompton, re-created the character of London row houses on Alta Vista Terrace. The street wall is designed as one unit but with an array of contrasts in color, rooflines, and style. There are twenty row houses on each side of the street. whose designs are mirrored diagonally across the block. All the row houses are two-story
building of Roman brick except the four three-story graystones in the center. In 1971 Alta Vista Terrace was designated Chicago’s first historic district. The distinctly human scale creates a unity and harmony rarely found elsewhere in the city.

Guests will have the entire place to themselves to enjoy.   There is a   Master Suite with a private  bathroom with a great soaking tub.    

A second bedroom with a very comfortable raised Air Mattress, along with a  bathroom with a huge shower. 


Access  to a  in house  washer and dryer is another added bonus.  

The Kitchen is fully equipped for guests  to cook meals, a microwave is provided to reheat leftovers, a table and chairs, fridge, stove, utensils etc...

Enjoy Free WiFi during your stay.    There is a workspace for your Laptop  or Tablet in the living  space.  Lounge couches and a dining area for your comfort also  located in the living space. 


Bath amenities are left for you to utilize if needed such as shampoo, conditioner, shower gel, hand soap, lotions, cotton balls, Q-tips  and more.  
We have a endless supply of bath towels, pillows, and bedding for your comfort.  If you left it at home, more than likely, we have provided it for you.


We welcome long term stays 30 days or more.

We look forward to sharing our place with you.   Feel free to contact us if there is anything we can do to make  your experience more pleasing.

Some Places to Visit in Chicago:

*  Millennium Park  *  Hyde Park Dining
*  Navy Pier.  * Musuem of Science

*  Magnificent Mile * Downtown Chicago



Have a wonderful day... and Welcome to Chicago!! 

Your Superhosts,
* Ade & J Shuntay *

description:

If cooking's not your thing, Logan Square has several award-winning restaurants– all nearby– or you can take the train (a 5-minute walk!) anywhere in the city to get a personal taste of Chicago. The space

neighborhood_overview: Cheap eats and bike-friendly streets. Gourmet coffee, scruffy dive bars and artisanal cocktail lounges. Some may say it's a recipe for a hipster haven but there's a proud, working-class sensibility that keeps this Northwest Side neighborhood grounded. In Logan Square, the strong neighborly connection is evident all around, from active preservation groups to community gardens and a locally-run farmers market. "Local" being the key word when describing many aspects of the scene: ingredients are sourced locally at their buzz-worthy restaurants; corner taps tout local, craft brews; galleries showcase local artists; and concerts and street fests promote local, upstart bands.
host_about:
We're both transplants from warmer places (Florida and California), but have been loving Chicago for over 10 years. We live a few blocks away, and spend as much time as we can in and around Logan Square.

Can't live without: Dark Matter coffee and the Logan Square Farmer's Market

Visitors to Chicago shouldn't miss: pizza and a beer at Middlebrow Bungalow, a cocktail at Billy Sunday, the architectural boat tours, and lazy walks through all the fun neighborhoods.

Designed as an ornate Spanish courtyard and completed in 1926, the Aragon Ballroom was one of the biggest entertainment venues for big bands in Chicago during the 1940s. Today, it’s used as a concert venue for rock, pop, and electronic music artists. With easy access to and from the El, the Aragon Ballroom is one of the most popular and certainly one of the most unique performance spaces in all of Chicago.

host_about:
Hello!  My name is Jennifer and I am the founder of Ovation Rentals, LLC which specializes in connecting hosts (including myself!) with guests looking for short- and long-term rental units in Chicago and Southwest Michigan.  We have something for everyone, from the unexpected visitor just needing a safe, comfortable place to rest her head to a family planning a big reunion on Lake Michigan.  

I am originally from Chicago, but when to college in UPENN in Philadelphia and also lived in New York before settling back in the Second City.  I have been a lover of travel for as long as I remember.  I took my first international trip  (to Paris!) when I was just 15 years old.  I made a deal with my dad that if I could save up the money for the flights by working 2 summer jobs then he would pay for the hotel and meals.  I worked my butt off that summer and we spent Christmas in Paris...and I was hooked on world travel!  Before Airbnb existed, I did much of my international travel via Home Exchange - where you exchange homes with a host family in another city (NOT the same as "couch surfing" lol).  I found that experiencing a new city like a local was infinitely more enjoyable than staying in a stuffy hotel, so when Airbnb came along I was overjoyed to have a new way to "live like a local!"  And eventually I evolved from just an Airbnb Traveler to an Airbnb Host.  

As a host I strive to help my guests experience all the things I love about the cities and towns that I love - the food, culture and  natural beauty - in comfortable accommodations that are reasonably priced.  I strive to do the same for the other hosts that I represent through Ovation.  Our goal is to make every guest feel truly at home!

neighborhood_overview: It is located between Hollywood and Ardmore Avenues, and in the past it has been referred to by both street names. A surprising amount of what is now Lincoln Park is made from landfill, and this landfill was completed in stages. Lincoln Park’s final landfill extension was completed in the 1950s between Foster and Ardmore Avenues, and the fill included a new beach at Ardmore Avenue. The beach is considered to be a part of Lincoln Park. Planning and design for the extension started in 1947, but construction and fill did not begin until three years later. The fill project continued over the majority of the decade, and it was finally finished in 1958. Osterman Beach is named for Kathy Osterman (1943-1992), a dedicated public servant who was beloved by her community. She served as Alderman for Edgewater, President of the Edgewater Community Council, and Director of the Mayor's Office of Special Events. In 1993, Ardmore Beach was renamed in her honor as Kathy Osterman Beach.

I am passionate about my students and I would like to take a group of inner city student to Europe.  This is one of my educational dreams.

We once drove from Chicago to New York for Christmas to see my family, then from New Your through Mexico, El Salvador and Guatemala to Honduras to see my son's father family and back to Chicago. host_about:
Hello! Thank you for visiting.  A little bit about our Airbnb journey:

In 2013,  David (my husband) and I met a Belizean from Placencia while living in New York.  He invited us to stay at his house in the Placencia Village and after one visit, we fell in love with the village, the people, the food, and the relaxing way of life in Placencia. We went back every year for a week and eventually purchased the original Toucan Lulu (which was shown on HGTV), transformed the old house into The Coconut House and built two high end bungalows. We are proud to offer modern amenities on a beautiful, relaxing oceanfront lot so that others can have the opportunity to experience the relaxing and amazing vacation that we had years ago.

We also just recently expanded our Airbnb portfolio and purchased and renovated the Leo Loft and The Grand Ave Apartments.  The Leo Loft is a spacious and art deco inspired 2 bed/2 bath apartment located in West Town Chicago, one of the premier live/work spaces anchoring Chicago's desirable West Loop neighborhood. The Grand Ave Apartments are 2 bed/1 baths Parisian/Scandinavian inspired apartments with a lovely backyard in the heart of the West Loop. We would love to host you in  Belize or Chicago and please let me know if you have any questions!
-Carolyn and David

Back of the Yards is an industrial and residential neighborhood so named because it was near the former Union Stock Yards, which employed thousands of European immigrants in the early 20th century. Life in this neighborhood was explored in Upton Sinclair's 1906 novel The Jungle. The area was formerly part of the town of Lake until it was annexed by Chicago in 1889. Officially part of the South Lawndale community area, the Little Village neighborhood is brimming with Mexican-American culture. Before it was known as “La Villita,” Little Village saw an influx of German, Czech, and Polish immigrants following the Great Chicago Fire of 1871. At that time, many people worked in the nearby factories, and it has been a working-class community ever since.

neighborhood_overview:
The Ravenswood Manor Historic District is a historic district in the Albany Park community area of North Side, Chicago, Illinois. It is bordered by the Chicago River on the East, and by the alley south of Lawrence Avenue on the North, Sacramento Avenue on the West, and the alley North of Montrose Avenue on the south.

Ravenswood Manor is a primarily residential neighborhood that was developed during the early twentieth century. It contains many bungalows, and some of the homes along the river have their own docks.

The district was added to the National Register of Historic Places on September 5, 2008.

Printers Row is “pocket” neighborhood just minutes from the Chicago Loop. After the Great Chicago Fire of 1871, the area became the Midwest hub of the printing industry with historically significant buildings designed by legendary architects like Daniel Burnham, William Holabird and William Le Baron Jenney. Today, many of those historic buildings remain but the quiet, tree lined streets are now largely residential. Of course, it continues to be a draw for fans of Chicago architecture.

During the day, the neighborhood is an easy walk to offices in the Loop, off Michigan Avenue, or in LaSalle Street financial centers. After hours, the district is alive with restaurants, boutiques, book and antique stores.

It boasts famous blues clubs, eclectic music venues and neighborhood taverns where residents gather. It also has an annual book fair: The Printers Row Book Fair gathers authors, poets, speakers and, of course, books.

It’s home to the lakefront Museum Campus, where you’ll find three of Chicago’s biggest museums. Also in the South Loop, you’ll find celebrated jazz clubs, a mix of crowd-pleasing restaurants, and vibrant historic areas like industrial Motor Row and charming the Prairie Avenue District.

The Gold Coast Historic District is a historic district in Chicago, Illinois. Part of Chicago's Near North Side community area, it is roughly bounded by North Avenue, Lake Shore Drive, Oak Street, and Clark Street.

The Gold Coast neighborhood grew in the wake of the Great Chicago Fire. In 1882, millionaire Potter Palmer moved to the area from the Prairie Avenue neighborhood on the city's south side. He filled in a swampy area which later became Lake Shore Drive, and built the Palmer Mansion, a forty-two room castle-like structure designed by Henry Ives Cobb and Charles Sumner Frost. Other wealthy Chicagoans followed Potter into the neighborhood, which became one of the richest in Chicago.

host_about:
I am a divorced father of four. That's my three youngest kids in the scooter sidecar with me. My oldest is all grown up and just graduated from law school in Texas. 
I worked for Apple. I currently consult with companies about technology/internet/social media/marketing/branding. We own the entire building and I work and live (some of the time) on the third floor with tenants on first floor. We use AirBnB for the Garden Apartment (totally private); the second floor is a hostel style AirBnB; and upstairs on the 3rd floor we have up to two bedrooms that are available when I don’t have my kids in town.
I enjoy going on bike rides to the beach with my kids, and my girlfriend and her kids. I love to read and I am a tech geek. I am a coffee OR tea drinker and after drinking both black for almost forty years, I have started using cream in them — a habit I picked up in Nairobi, Kenya a couple years ago when I was doing some missionary work (plus my girlfriend uses cream and so I have no choice). 
If I had to pick some things I can't live without: my girlfriend (and her boys); my kids; my technology; my morning coffee; my fellowship; and my friends. And I love to watch movies. Old. New. Comedy. Mystery. Action. It doesn't matter. I like them all. 
I enjoy working out — lifting weights and riding a bike, plus I am a life-long swimmer. I also just started playing hockey! At age 52! Crazy. 
We have been hosting guests for over five years now. We have over 250 reviews 98% are 5 star. We are a SuperHost. We love this. And we are really good at it.
I am a pretty laid back guy. I like things to be neat and tidy, but it's hard to do without motivation. AirBnB has been the motivation to get our place all tricked out and we are very proud of it. We hope you will enjoy staying here. All of our units are in a great neighborhood—in a great city. We have lots of suggestions for fun stuff to do, not the typical touristy stuff, but cool Chicago things that Chicagoans like to do/see.

As I am getting older I have decided that I really want to travel and see more of the world...but limited finances (coupled with my refusal to sit int he back of planes) as well as a desire to really get to see how people live and just not how tourists are treated makes this a great option for me!

neighborhood_overview:
Fun fact—the Loop is the 2nd largest commercial district in the US after Midtown Manhattan.

The Loop is the heart of the city and it’s bursting with iconic Chicago attractions, including historic architecture, river cruises, Millennium Park, the Chicago Riverwalk, a vibrant theatre district, incredible dining, shopping along State Street…and that’s just for starters.

The Loop is also home to the award-winning Chicago Riverwalk, a pedestrian-only pathway lined with great waterfront restaurants, the McCormick Bridgehouse & Chicago River Museum, and the mind-blowing digital art display Art on theMART.

On the lakefront side of the Loop, you’ll also find the Millennium Park Campus — home to iconic Cloud Gate (aka “The Bean”), Crown Fountain, Lurie Garden, and the Jay Pritzker Pavilion that hosts legendary music festivals like the Chicago Blues Festival, Chicago Jazz Festival, and a free summer music series and film series. host_about:
Hello! Thank you for visiting.  A little bit about our Airbnb journey:

In 2013,  David (my husband) and I met a Belizean from Placencia while living in New York.  He invited us to stay at his house in the Placencia Village and after one visit, we fell in love with the village, the people, the food, and the relaxing way of life in Placencia. We went back every year for a week and eventually purchased the original Toucan Lulu (which was shown on HGTV), transformed the old house into The Coconut House and built two high end bungalows. We are proud to offer modern amenities on a beautiful, relaxing oceanfront lot so that others can have the opportunity to experience the relaxing and amazing vacation that we had years ago.

We also just recently expanded our Airbnb portfolio and purchased and renovated the Leo Loft and The Grand Ave Apartments.  The Leo Loft is a spacious and art deco inspired 2 bed/2 bath apartment located in West Town Chicago, one of the premier live/work spaces anchoring Chicago's desirable West Loop neighborhood. The Grand Ave Apartments are 2 bed/1 baths Parisian/Scandinavian inspired apartments with a lovely backyard in the heart of the West Loop. We would love to host you in  Belize or Chicago and please let me know if you have any questions!
-Carolyn and David
